summary: Olle Qvarnström is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Washington, Harvard University, and the University of Copenhagen, working under Tord Olsson, Karl H. Potter, Collett Cox, and Christian Lindtner, and held a post at Lund University.
Olli Littunen works in Indology and religious studies. Littunen is a PhD candidate at Leiden University studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Om Prakash worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma and Bisheshwar Prasad, later teaching there, at Kirori Mal College, and as professor of economic history at Delhi School of Economics.

On Shionoya was a Sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (c. 1903–1906) and the University of Leipzig (c. 1912–1914). He held a post at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1920 to 1938.
Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Orna Almogi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. She has held posts at the University of Hamburg and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Osamu Hayashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg. He held professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.
Osamu Izumoji is a scholar in sinology and other fields. He held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. After studying at Kansai University (c. 1949–1953), he held posts at Kansai University (c. 1957–1998), Kogakkan University (c. 1998–2002), and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Baiei Henmi and served as the director of the fine arts department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.

Osborn Bergin was a linguist who studied at University College Cork, the School of Irish Learning, and the University of Freiburg under Kuno Meyer and Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at University College Dublin (c. 1909–1940) and DIAS.

Oskar von Hinüber is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist who studied at Mainz, Tübingen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg under Paul Thieme. He held posts at the University of Mainz, directed the Nepal Research Centre, and served as professor at Freiburg.

Osmund Bopearachchi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, Panthéon-Sorbonne, and Paris-Sorbonne under Paul Bernard and Jean-Marie Dentzer, later holding posts at CNRS and UC Berkeley.

Osvald Sirén was a Sinologist and art historian who completed his doctorate at the University of Helsinki. He was a professor at Stockholm University (1908–1923), lectured at Harvard and Yale, and served as a curator at Paris's Musée Guimet and Stockholm's Nationalmuseum.

Othmar Frank was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Paris. He held teaching posts at Banz Abbey, Kaiser-Heinrich-Gymnasium Bamberg, and professorships at the universities of Bamberg, Würzburg, and Munich.
Otoya Tanaka was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji from around 1924 to 1927. He later served as a professor at Chuo University from 1951 to 1974.

Otto Blau was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Between 1848 and 1852, he studied at the University of Halle, the University of Leipzig, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott.

Otto Fischer was a Sinologist and art historian who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen. He served as director of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart and Kunstmuseum Basel, and was an art history professor at the University of Basel (c. 1927–1937).

Otto Franke was a scholar of sinology and Indology who studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held the chair of Chinese Language and Culture at Hamburg and served as professor of sinology at Humboldt University of Berlin.
